$comment: SPFx version -> supported Node.js majors, transcribed from Microsoft's own compatibility
reference. This is DATA, not a compiled-in table, so a newer SPFx release can be taught to an
existing build without waiting for a Tamp.Spfx release: point SpfxNodeSupport.LoadFrom at your
Keys are the SPFx version exactly as that table lists it. A project's version is matched exactly
first, then by falling back to its major.minor, then its major — so 1.24.2 resolves against 1.24
and a new patch does not read as unknown. Values are Node MAJORS only: the table's 'v16.13+'
qualifier is recorded in minimumMinor rather than being flattened away.
Where patches within one minor differ, the minor entry carries the NARROWER set and the wider
one is listed at its exact patch: 1.8.0/1.8.1 support Node 8 while 1.8.2 adds 10, and 1.4.0
supports Node 6 while 1.4.1 adds 8. Collapsing those upward would claim support Microsoft does
not, which is the one direction this file must never fail in.
